title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: 5.5 Constraints
subcategory: PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, CHECK, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, EXCLUDE
core_concepts: CHECK passes on true or NULL
engineering_principles: MANDATORY: CHECK expressions must be immutable and must not reference other rows or tables. RECOMMENDED: the majority of columns should be NOT NULL; every table should have a primary key (not enforced, usually best practice); index referencing columns yourself because they are not indexed automatically. Choose CASCADE for dependent components, RESTRICT or NO ACTION for independent objects, SET NULL or SET DEFAULT for optional relationships.
practical_examples: price numeric CHECK (price > 0); CONSTRAINT valid_discount CHECK (price > discounted_price); UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (product_no); product_no integer REFERENCES products ON DELETE RESTRICT; FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, author_id) REFERENCES users ON DELETE SET NULL (author_id); EXCLUDE USING gist (c WITH &&).
why_it_matters: Primary reference for declaring integrity rules in PostgreSQL DDL and for choosing foreign key behavior.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation from the PostgreSQL project.
notes: Covers PostgreSQL 18.6. Deferral details are on the SET CONSTRAINTS reference page.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: 8.1 Numeric Types
engineering_principles: MANDATORY for money: use numeric because floating-point types are inexact. RECOMMENDED: integer as the default integer type, bigint when its range is insufficient. Trade-off: numeric calculations are very slow compared with integer and floating-point types. Serial columns do not automatically get UNIQUE or PRIMARY KEY.
practical_examples: Serial expands to an integer NOT NULL column with DEFAULT nextval(...) backed by an owned sequence; the page demonstrates rounding differences with round(x::numeric) versus round(x::double precision).
why_it_matters: Sets the type choice for monetary and exact quantities and explains the limits of serial key columns.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation from the PostgreSQL project.
notes: Covers PostgreSQL 18.6. The page does not state a preference for identity columns over serial.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: 8.5 Date/Time Types
core_concepts: timestamp with time zone stored as UTC
timestamp without time zone ignores zone
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: use date/time types containing both date and time when using time zones; time with time zone is not recommended because offsets cannot adapt to daylight-saving changes. Designers must know the original zone of a timestamptz input is not retained.
practical_examples: TIMESTAMP '2004-10-19 10:23:54+02' is timestamp without time zone, while TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE '2004-10-19 10:23:54+02' is zone-aware.
why_it_matters: Defines how instants are stored and why column type choice affects correctness across time zones.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation from the PostgreSQL project.
notes: Covers PostgreSQL 18.6. The wiki Don't Do This page is stricter about timestamp without time zone.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: 8.14 JSON Types
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: most applications should prefer jsonb; keep a somewhat fixed document structure; limit documents to a manageable size because any update locks the whole row; model each document as an atomic datum.
practical_examples: CREATE INDEX idxgin ON api USING GIN (jdoc); CREATE INDEX idxginp ON api USING GIN (jdoc jsonb_path_ops); CREATE INDEX idxgintags ON api USING GIN ((jdoc -> 'tags'));
why_it_matters: Gives official criteria for storing and indexing JSON alongside relational columns.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation from the PostgreSQL project.
notes: Covers PostgreSQL 18.6.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: 11.2 Index Types
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: B-tree fits the most common situations; hash handles only equality; GIN suits values with multiple components; BRIN is most effective for columns well correlated with physical row order; GiST and SP-GiST support specialized strategies.
practical_examples: CREATE INDEX name ON table USING HASH (column); SELECT * FROM places ORDER BY location <-> point '(101,456)' LIMIT 10;
why_it_matters: Maps query operators and data shapes to the correct PostgreSQL index method.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation from the PostgreSQL project.
notes: Covers PostgreSQL 18.6. BRIN is framed by physical correlation, not table size.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: 5.12 Table Partitioning
engineering_principles: MANDATORY: unique and primary key constraints must include all partition key columns, and those keys cannot contain expressions. CONTEXTUAL: partitioning is normally worthwhile only for very large tables, with a rule of thumb of exceeding server physical memory. RECOMMENDED: partition on columns common in WHERE clauses and align partitions with bulk removal.
practical_examples: CREATE TABLE measurement (...) PARTITION BY RANGE (logdate); CREATE TABLE measurement_y2006m02 PARTITION OF measurement FOR VALUES FROM ('2006-02-01') TO ('2006-03-01'); ALTER TABLE measurement DETACH PARTITION measurement_y2006m02 CONCURRENTLY;
why_it_matters: Defines when partitioning pays off and which key design limits it imposes.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation from the PostgreSQL project.
notes: Covers PostgreSQL 18.6. The source says warehouse workloads can use more partitions than OLTP. The fetched extract did not cover foreign keys referencing partitioned tables.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: 5.9 Row Security Policies
engineering_principles: MANDATORY awareness: superusers and BYPASSRLS roles always bypass RLS, owners bypass it unless forced, and unique, primary key and foreign key checks ignore row security, which can leak information through covert channels.
practical_examples: ALTER TABLE accounts ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; CREATE POLICY account_managers ON accounts TO managers USING (manager = current_user); CREATE POLICY admin_local_only ON passwd AS RESTRICTIVE TO admin USING (pg_catalog.inet_client_addr() IS NULL);
why_it_matters: Enables tenant and row isolation in the schema and documents its failure modes.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation from the PostgreSQL project.
notes: Covers PostgreSQL 18.6.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: 13.2 Transaction Isolation
engineering_principles: MANDATORY: applications using Repeatable Read or Serializable must be prepared to retry whole transactions after serialization failures. RECOMMENDED for Serializable: declare READ ONLY when possible, keep transactions small, avoid idle-in-transaction sessions and sequential scans.
practical_examples: Serialization failures report ERROR: could not serialize access due to concurrent update, or due to read/write dependencies among transactions; failures use SQLSTATE '40001'.
why_it_matters: Determines which invariants need constraints, locks or retries at each isolation level.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation from the PostgreSQL project.
notes: Covers PostgreSQL 18.6. Read Uncommitted behaves as Read Committed.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: 4.1 Lexical Structure (Identifiers and Key Words)
engineering_principles: MANDATORY consistency: unquoted names fold to lower case and quoted names are case-sensitive, so always quote a particular name or never quote it. Identifiers over NAMEDATALEN-1 bytes are truncated.
practical_examples: FOO, foo and "foo" are the same identifier, while "Foo" and "FOO" are different. UPDATE "my_table" SET "a" = 5;
why_it_matters: Provides the hard rules a naming standard must respect in PostgreSQL.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation from the PostgreSQL project.
notes: Covers PostgreSQL 18.6. Not a naming-convention standard; no official one was found.

title: Don't Do This
subcategory: Schema, type, SQL and authentication practices
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: prefer identity columns, timestamptz, text with CHECK constraints where validation is real, numeric with a separate currency column, and lowercase names with underscores. Avoid NOT IN, BETWEEN with timestamps, rules, table inheritance and trust authentication over TCP/IP.
practical_examples: Use >= start and < next period start instead of BETWEEN for timestamps; use date_trunc('second', ...) instead of timestamp(0); use text with a CHECK constraint or a domain instead of char(n).
why_it_matters: Concise project-hosted list of schema anti-patterns with reasons and narrow exceptions.
authority_rationale: Hosted on the official PostgreSQL wiki and maintained by contributors, but it is not part of the reviewed manual.
notes: Date is the page's last edit. It is more prescriptive than the manual on serial, varchar(n) and timestamp without time zone.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: 25.3 Continuous Archiving and Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR)
engineering_principles: MANDATORY: archive commands must return zero only on success and must not overwrite existing files; pg_dump cannot serve as the base for WAL replay. RECOMMENDED: test archiving before the first base backup, monitor the archiver, retain several backup sets and back up configuration files separately.
practical_examples: wal_level = replica; archive_mode = on; archive_command = 'test ! -f /mnt/server/archivedir/%f && cp %p /mnt/server/archivedir/%f'; pg_basebackup -D /backup/base -X stream -c fast; restore_command = 'cp /mnt/server/archivedir/%f %p'.
why_it_matters: Defines the official recovery path that schema and operations standards must assume.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation from the PostgreSQL project.
notes: Covers PostgreSQL 18.6. This method restores the entire cluster.

title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: 17.6.2.1 Clustered and Secondary Indexes
core_concepts: secondary indexes contain primary key columns
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: define a primary key for each table; add an auto-increment column if no logical unique non-null key exists; keep the primary key short because secondary indexes store it.
practical_examples: InnoDB selects the PRIMARY KEY, then the first UNIQUE index whose key columns are all NOT NULL, then a hidden GEN_CLUST_INDEX on a 6-byte row ID.
why_it_matters: Explains why primary key choice affects physical layout and every secondary index in InnoDB.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation from Oracle's MySQL team.
notes: Covers MySQL 8.4. It does not discuss UUIDs or page splits.

title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: 13.2.2 The DATE, DATETIME, and TIMESTAMP Types
engineering_principles: MANDATORY awareness: TIMESTAMP is converted to UTC for storage and back for retrieval, while DATETIME is not, so a changed session time zone changes retrieved TIMESTAMP values. TIMESTAMP ends at 2038-01-19 03:14:07 UTC.
practical_examples: SELECT col, CAST(col AT TIME ZONE INTERVAL '+00:00' AS DATETIME) AS ut FROM ts ORDER BY id;
why_it_matters: Drives the choice between time-zone-normalized TIMESTAMP and wider-range DATETIME columns.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation from Oracle's MySQL team.
notes: Covers MySQL 8.4. It does not recommend one type over the other.

title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: 15.1.20.5 FOREIGN KEY Constraints
core_concepts: NO ACTION equals RESTRICT in InnoDB
engineering_principles: MANDATORY: parent and child must use the same storage engine, and fixed-precision types must match in size and sign. InnoDB rejects SET DEFAULT, rejects parent changes immediately under NO ACTION, and does not support foreign keys on user-partitioned tables. Re-enabling foreign_key_checks does not recheck existing rows.
practical_examples: FOREIGN KEY (product_category, product_id) REFERENCES product(category, id) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT.
why_it_matters: Defines MySQL referential integrity limits that differ materially from PostgreSQL.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation from Oracle's MySQL team.
notes: Covers MySQL 8.4. NDB can perform deferred checks with NO ACTION; InnoDB cannot.

title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: 15.1.20.6 CHECK Constraints
engineering_principles: MANDATORY awareness: only FALSE violates a CHECK, so NULL passes. Expressions cannot use AUTO_INCREMENT columns, other tables, nondeterministic functions, stored functions, variables or subqueries. IGNORE statements turn violations into warnings and skip the row.
practical_examples: c2 INT CONSTRAINT c2_positive CHECK (c2 > 0); CONSTRAINT c1_nonzero CHECK (c1 <> 0); unnamed constraints receive names such as t1_chk_1.
why_it_matters: Documents what MySQL CHECK constraints can guarantee and where they can be bypassed.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation from Oracle's MySQL team.
notes: Covers MySQL 8.4. Enforcement since 8.0.16 (2019-04-25) comes from the 8.0.16 release notes, not this page.

title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: 26.6 Restrictions and Limitations on Partitioning
core_concepts: no foreign keys on partitioned InnoDB tables
engineering_principles: MANDATORY: partitioned InnoDB tables cannot have or be the target of foreign keys, and partition keys must follow the documented type rules. RECOMMENDED: never change the SQL mode after creating partitioned tables.
practical_examples: SUBPARTITION BY KEY requires an explicit column, for example SUBPARTITION BY KEY(id); RANGE COLUMNS and LIST COLUMNS allow string, DATE and DATETIME columns.
why_it_matters: Partitioning in MySQL forces a trade-off against declared referential integrity.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation from Oracle's MySQL team.
notes: Covers MySQL 8.4. The unique-key rule is on the linked section 26.6.1.

title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: 11.2.3 Identifier Case Sensitivity
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: consistently create and reference databases and tables with lowercase names; for InnoDB portability use lower_case_table_names=1 on all platforms. MANDATORY: the setting cannot be changed after server initialization.
practical_examples: SELECT col_name FROM tbl_name AS a WHERE a.col_name = 1 OR A.col_name = 2; fails on Unix because it refers to the alias with different case.
why_it_matters: Identifier case behavior can break schema portability across operating systems.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation from Oracle's MySQL team.
notes: Covers MySQL 8.4. Not a full naming-convention standard; no official one was found.

title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: 17.7.2.1 Transaction Isolation Levels
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: do not mix locking and non-locking statements in one REPEATABLE READ transaction. MANDATORY constraint: READ COMMITTED supports only row-based binary logging.
practical_examples: With CREATE TABLE t (a INT NOT NULL, b INT) ENGINE = InnoDB, session A's UPDATE t SET b = 5 WHERE b = 3 blocks session B's UPDATE t SET b = 4 WHERE b = 2 under REPEATABLE READ, but B proceeds under READ COMMITTED.
why_it_matters: InnoDB's default isolation and locking differ from PostgreSQL's and affect portable concurrency design.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation from Oracle's MySQL team.
notes: Covers MySQL 8.4.

title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: 9.2 Database Backup Methods
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: use --single-transaction for online mysqldump backups of InnoDB; use binary logs for incremental backups; back up replica metadata repositories with replica data. MANDATORY awareness: copying table files does not work for InnoDB because modified data may remain unflushed in memory.
practical_examples: mysqldump --single-transaction --all-databases > backup.sql; FLUSH LOGS; FLUSH TABLES tbl_list WITH READ LOCK;
why_it_matters: Summarizes the official MySQL backup options and the limits of each.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation from Oracle's MySQL team.
notes: Covers MySQL 8.4. Binary logging is enabled by default in 8.4. The page does not cover MySQL Shell dump utilities.

title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: 17.1.2 Best Practices for InnoDB Tables
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: specify a primary key for every table using the most frequently queried columns or an auto-increment value; define foreign keys on join columns with identical types; group related DML into transactions; avoid LOCK TABLES.
practical_examples: Use START TRANSACTION and COMMIT around related DML; use SELECT ... FOR UPDATE to lock only the rows to be updated; run with --sql_mode=NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION.
why_it_matters: Vendor's short checklist connecting key choice, foreign keys and transaction use for InnoDB.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation from Oracle's MySQL team.
notes: Covers MySQL 8.4. The page gives no general data type guidance beyond matching join column types.
